1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	Guidance for working in this repository.
4	
5	## Project
6	
7	Spring PetClinic REST, converted from Spring `@RestController` classes to
8	**OfficeFloor function injection**. Spring's DI, security, persistence and DTOs are
9	unchanged; only the request handling is now explicit function orchestration.
10	
11	<!-- https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md -->
12	@AGENTS.md
13

1	## OfficeFloor REST endpoints
2	
3	Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
4	OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
5	pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.
6	
7	- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
8	  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
9	  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
10	  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
11	- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
12	  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
13	- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
14	- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
15	- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
16	- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.
17	
18	### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`
19	
20	The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.
21	
22	`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`
23	
24	```yaml
25	# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
26	# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
27	validate:
28	  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
29	  next: load
30	load:
31	  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
32	  next: apply
33	apply:
34	  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
35	  govern: [ transaction ]
36	  next: save
37	save:
38	  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
39	  govern: [ transaction ]
40	  next: respond
41	respond:
42	  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
43	```
44	
45	```java
46	// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
47	public class ValidateOwner {
48	  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
49	    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
50	  }
51	}
52	public class LoadOwner {
53	  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
54	      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
55	    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
56	    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
57	    ownerOut.set(owner);
58	  }
59	}
60	public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
61	  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
62	    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
63	    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
64	  }
65	}
66	public class SaveOwner {
67	  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
68	    repository.save(owner);
69	  }
70	}
71	public class RespondWithOwner {
72	  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
73	    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
74	  }
75	}
76	```
77	
78	`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`
79	
80	```yaml
81	handle:
82	  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
83	```
84	
85	```java
86	public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
87	  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
88	      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
89	    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
90	  }
91	}
92	```
93	
94	### Step wiring
95	
96	Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
97	point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
98	method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
99	`method:`.
100	
101	- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
102	  as `@Parameter T`.
103	- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
104	  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
105	  branch; not calling it short-circuits.
106	
107	### Function parameters
108	
109	Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:
110	
111	- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
112	- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
113	- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
114	  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
115	  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
116	- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
117	  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.
118	
119	### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`
120	
121	Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
122	into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):
123	
124	- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
125	- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
126	  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
127	- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
128	  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.
129	
130	### Naming
131	
132	Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
133	absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
134	publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
135	`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).
136	
137	Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
138	responder. Steps in between work with entities.
139	
140	### Request body and validation
141	
142	- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
143	  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
144	  first step publishes it as a variable.
145	- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
146	  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
147	  invalid body can return 400.
148	
149	### Transactions
150	
151	`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
152	listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
153	the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.
154	
155	### Errors
156	
157	Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
158	Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
159	`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
160	`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
161	anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.
162	
163	### Security
164	
165	Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:
166	
167	```yaml
168	composition:
169	  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
170	```
171	
172	- Full reference: https://officefloor.net/llms.txt
173

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            The optional honorific title of the pet owner. When present it is one
            of 'MR', 'MRS', 'MS' or 'DR'. Stored and returned, and used to derive
            the owner's 'salutation'.
          type: string
          pattern: "^(MR|MRS|MS|DR)$"
          example: DR
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted as a flat single line for
            backward compatibility; when the structured 'addressLine1'/'addressLine2'
            fields are supplied they are preferred and this field is returned as the
            composed, normalized address (normalized addressLine1, plus a single space
            and the normalized addressLine2 when addressLine2 is present).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the pet owner's structured postal address (street number
            and name). Preferred over the flat 'address' when a non-blank value is
            supplied. Normalized like 'address' (trimmed, internal whitespace collapsed,
            upper-cased, common street-type abbreviations expanded) and stored/returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the structured postal address (unit, suite,
            etc.). When present it is normalized and appended to the composed 'address'
            after a single space; stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apt 4'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The optional 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. When present it must be
            four digits and valid for the owner's city per a fixed city-to-region
            table (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known
            region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Validated only when present; stored
            and returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
          example: '2000'
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and
            country code are kept, otherwise '+61' is assumed and a single leading
            '0' is dropped from the national digits. The result must carry 8 to 15
            digits after the '+'. The normalized E.164 value is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The optional date of birth of the pet owner, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'
            format. When present it is stored and returned, and is used to derive
            the owner's ageBand.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            When omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Create-time hint that this owner deliberately shares a household with an
            existing owner. The household is keyed on (lastName, postcode) and drives
            only the derived householdId, household size and membership-level cap. It no
            longer affects duplicate detection, which is now keyed solely on the
            identityKey (SHA-256 of normalizedTelephone|lowerEmail|soundex(lastName)):
            an exact identityKey match is rejected 409, while a near match
            (same soundex(lastName) and postcode, different identityKey) is flagged as a
            possible duplicate. It does not create the household link; the shared
            householdId is always derived deterministically. Not persisted.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The pet owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,
                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            selfLink:
              title: Self link
              description: >-

## Summary

I implemented the `riskFlag` feature following the codebase's existing derived-flag pattern (mirroring `capacityWarning`).

`riskFlag` is `true` when **any** of three soft signals holds, else `false`:
1. **Possible duplicate** — the persisted `possibleDuplicate` flag (set at creation by `DetectOwnerPossibleDuplicate`).
2. **Disposable-adjacent email** — the email's second-level label matches a known disposable provider (`mailinator`, `tempmail`, `guerrillamail`) under a different TLD/subdomain, without being an exact blocklist entry (those are already rejected 400 and never persist). This is the soft near-miss of the hard `ValidateOwnerEmailDomain` gate.
3. **City over soft capacity** — the city holds strictly more than `SOFT_CAPACITY` (40) owners, counted via the same `CheckOwnerCityCapacity.countInCity` population the hard 50-owner gate and capacity warning use.

Changes:
- **`Owner.java`** — added a `@Transient Boolean riskFlag` with getter/setter.
- **`CheckOwnerCityCapacity.java`** — added the `SOFT_CAPACITY = 40` constant (soft counterpart to the hard `CITY_CAPACITY = 50`).
- **`ValidateOwnerEmailDomain.java`** — added a static `isDisposableAdjacent(String email)` helper, keeping the disposable-domain knowledge single-sourced with the existing blocklist.
- **`DeriveOwnerRiskFlag.java`** (new) — combines the three signals; repo-backed for the city count.

- **`openapi.yml`** — added the read-only `riskFlag` boolean to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` gains the field and MapStruct auto-maps it.

The normal-owner case (unique city, no email) correctly yields `riskFlag: false`, satisfying the `coreRiskFlagFalseNormally` acceptance test.
